question.text: A body is thrown upward so that its position vector, in metres, changes with time t (in seconds) as r = 3t î + (4t − 5t²)ĵ. Find the time at which its y-coordinate becomes zero, and the x-coordinate of the body at that time.

solution.approach: Read the y-coordinate directly from the given position vector, set it to zero, and solve for the non-zero time; then use that time in the x-coordinate.

steps.text: Read the y-coordinate as a function of time from the position vector.
Set the y-coordinate to zero and factor.
Take the non-zero root, since t = 0 is the starting instant.
Substitute this time into the x-coordinate.

common_mistakes.text: Setting the rate of change of y to zero, instead of y itself, finds the time of the highest point (0.4 s) and gives a wrong x-coordinate of 1.2 m.
